question.problem:
Find the solution to the following initial value problem.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 10\end{aligned}]
$$

current_example.problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118414/assets/e2b30e84730a7fce6a66a38a1b3f6c387f2256c185d38e8af6fa8d388f3512d1.svg)

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda_1=2$ and $\lambda_2=-3.$*
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's construct the matrix differential equation $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)$ for the given system
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118414/assets/7c2de86789e83d14dc27db157cd16838174918985fe8da4952c725e6448d7637.svg)

- We are given that the eigenvalues are

$$
\lambda_1= 2
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\lambda_2= -3.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For $\lambda_1 =2,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118414/assets/f79799cff3d6c56cb61306405cf0c9adb365fdc16d501e22e884cddbd433abd3.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118414/assets/876267eb573680f6815c1e7ae40f5be5476ce72159e4daa8c12b303f12ae1b93.svg)

- For $\lambda_2 =-3,$ we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118414/assets/2c1c016b5be5214af2d8882713326ff3b8376e812106e8c6cb2c9c359599a1f2.svg)
So, we get an eigenvector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118414/assets/5bfc0f1b82bd124443e7f5d13124712810c03b8d600dd2930b02bd57ab79f6e8.svg)

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the values of $c_1$ and $c_2,$ we substitute $t=0$ in the general solution and use the initial values:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]{e}^{0} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}+6{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}=5 \\ {c}_{1}+6{c}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting the first equation from the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5{c}_{2}=-5\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $c_2 = -1$ into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}-1=5\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =6[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 6\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}.\end{aligned}
$$
